title: Loops
bridge: C has `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)`, `while (cond)` and `do { } while (cond);`, with `break` and `continue`. There's no for-each: you loop with an index. Arduino's `loop()` is itself called over and over by a hidden loop.

exercises.title: Sum to n
exercises.prompt: Write int sum_to(int n) that returns 1 + 2 + ... + n (0 if n is less than 1). Use a loop.

tests.why: Use a loop for this one.

hints: Start a total at 0 and add i each round.
for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) total += i;

exercises.title: Countdown
exercises.prompt: Read a number n, print n down to 1 (one per line), then Go!

quiz.q: A do-while body runs at least...
quiz.why: The check is at the end.

quiz.q: Does C have a for-each loop?
quiz.why: Arrays don't know their own length in C.

cards.q: Loop that runs at least once?

explain: Explain loops to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
